If knowledge is adorned with action, by complying with commands, avoiding prohibitions, and purifying the inner self, then the elevation is according to that measure; and if it is otherwise, then likewise. He placed the prepositional phrase and what it governs first, although His knowledge of all things is on one equal footing, to draw attention to the greater care given to deeds, especially the inward ones of faith and knowledge, which are the greatest spirit, because the situation involves a person moving from his place through making room, lowering, and raising, and the soul's share that drives one to run after deceits in that is not hidden (p-378). Hence it is deserving of greater warning. The occasion of revelation of the verse was that when the people of knowledge were more entitled to the head of the assembly, because they were more retentive of what the speaker of the assembly says, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Let those of you who have maturity and understanding sit next to me." "And the Prophet (ﷺ) used to honor the people of Badr among the Emigrants and the Helpers. Some people of Badr came, among them Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, and others had already preceded them to the assembly. They stood in front of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' The Prophet (ﷺ) returned their greeting. Then they greeted the people, and they returned their greeting. Then they stood on their feet, waiting for room to be made for them, but they did not do so. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said to those around him from [among] those who were not of Badr: 'Stand up, O so-and-so, and you, O so-and-so.' He made some of the assembly rise to the number of the newcomers from the people of Badr. That grieved those who were made to rise, and the Prophet (ﷺ) perceived dislike in their faces. The hypocrites said: 'Do you not claim that your companion is just? By Allah, he has not been just to these people. A people took their seats and loved closeness to their Prophet, so he made them rise and seated whoever came late in their place.' So Allah revealed this verse." And the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "A man should not make a man rise from his assembly and then sit in it himself, but make room, and Allah will make room for you." Related by Muslim from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both. And al-Ḥasan said: It reached me "that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought the polytheists and arranged his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, for battle, they competed for the first row. A man would say to his brothers: 'Make room so we may meet the enemy and attain martyrdom.' They would not make room for him, out of desire for jihad and martyrdom. So Allah revealed this verse." It indicates that if the righteous person dislikes being neighbor to a wicked person, he is prevented from living beside him, because he harms him and distracts him from many of his important affairs. The Prophet (ﷺ) has said: "There is no harm and no reciprocating harm." And he said: "I seek refuge in You from an evil neighbor in a permanent abode, for the neighbor of the desert moves on." And he said: "The worst of people is one whose neighbor does not feel safe from his evils."

Then He, exalted is He, said, magnifying His Messenger (ﷺ), forbidding burdening him (ﷺ) with questions and private conferring, and benefiting the poor, and distinguishing between the sincere and the hypocrite, and the lover of the Hereafter and the lover of this world,

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 12:

When He forbade what grieves through speech and conduct, and the prohibition on private conversation (*najwa*) was only to protect the heart of the Messenger ﷺ from what troubles it, the verse turns to their private conversations with him apart from that concern. This implies that their private conversations with him are not blameworthy. Many of them would speak privately with him with no aim except to show off by doing so, and they went to excess in this until it burdened him ﷺ. What benefits a person is only the speech of one who is suited to him in qualities and similar to him in character. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the person most averse to this world (*dunya*), out of his hatred for what Allah hates in it. (p-380) He commanded whoever wished to converse privately with him to give charity, so that this would be a sign of striving to adopt his pure character, which turns away from this world and turns toward Allah, and a demonstration to Him of his having previously turned toward the world [toward it]. Charity is a proof of sincerity in faith. It would also lighten for him ﷺ the burden of the many private conversations they had made excessive, so that only one whose faith is sound would converse with him, and he would give charity. This would be a preface to his benefiting from that conversation [just as a gift prepares one for acceptance, as has been reported: "What a fine gift is one given before need"]. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, those who claim that they have made this reality exist, whether rich or poor. ﴿When you consult privately with the Messenger﴾, meaning, when you wish to converse privately with ﴿the Messenger﴾ ﷺ, meaning the one who has no superior in messengership. He is the most perfect of creation, and his function requires that speech come from him with what the King (Allah) has sent him with, and that his dignity prevent anyone from beginning speech with him. So there is nothing for the one he addresses except to act by compliance and nothing else. ﴿then offer charity﴾, meaning, by reason of this lofty intention, as an obligation. He likened private conversation to a person who has two hands and needs to purify himself so as to be fit to draw near to the Messenger ﷺ, so He said: ﴿before your private conversation﴾, meaning (p-381) before your secret which you wish to use to raise yourselves, ﴿charity﴾ which will be for you a decisive proof of your sincerity, as has been reported: "Charity is a proof." It attests for you to your claim of faith, which is affirming Allah, exalted is He, and His Messenger ﷺ, and everything that came from Allah, exalted is He, and the greatest part of it is turning away from this world and turning toward the Hereafter. For this reason He began a new statement: ﴿That﴾, meaning, this very lofty character of offering charity before private conversation, ﴿is best for you﴾ — O best of creation. Perhaps He addressed him alone with this address because no one else knows all the secrets in it.

He returned to the first point and said: ﴿and purer﴾, meaning, for your religion, than refraining from charity. ﴿and purer﴾, because charity is purification, growth, and increase in every good, and for this reason it is called *zakat* (purifying alms). ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawba: 103]. The expression with the comparative form (*afal*) is because they are already purified by faith before it.

When He had commanded this, and it was His custom not to impose what is beyond capacity, to lighten the burden on His servants, especially this community, He said: ﴿But if you do not find﴾, meaning, what you would offer in advance.

Since the sufficient meaning of lightening was: "then there is nothing upon you," He indicated it with something better than that, and He said: ﴿then indeed Allah﴾, meaning the One to whom belong all attributes of perfection. He emphasized it to exclude the likelihood of such a thing, since what is known of a king, when he imposes something on his subjects, is that he does not remove it (p-382) at all, especially if it is slight. It indicates that He, glorified is He, will not impose what is beyond ability, by His saying: ﴿Forgiving, Merciful﴾, meaning, He has the two attributes of concealing faults and honoring by manifesting good qualities, and both are constant. So He forgives and shows mercy, at times by not punishing the disobedient, and at times by granting ease to the constrained by abrogating what is burdensome [to what is lighter]. It has been said that this verse was abrogated (*nusikha*) before it was acted upon. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "No one acted on it except me. I wished to converse privately and had a dinar, so I exchanged it for ten dirhams and conversed with him ten times, giving a dirham in charity each time. Then the hardship of this became apparent to the people, so the concession to abandon charity was revealed." Al-Nasa'i in *al-Kubra* and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan gharib," and Ibn Hibban, Abu Ya'la, and al-Bazzar related from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Command them to give charity.' I said: 'How much, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A dinar.' I said: 'They cannot bear it.' He said: 'Then half a dinar.' I said: 'They cannot bear it.' He said: 'Then how much?' I said: 'A barley-grain.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'You are indeed austere.' So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive?﴾ [al-Mujadila: 13], the verse." ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "Through me Allah lightened this community." That no one else acted upon it does not discredit it, since it is possible that they did not find anything at the time of private conversation, or that [they] did not need (p-383) to converse privately.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 13:

When the ending of the verse indicated facilitation, and some claimants might falsely pretend they lacked the means, thereby falling into hardship, and since He, exalted is He, is intensely solicitous for the salvation of this Community, He indicated His gentleness toward them by abrogating the obligation after imposing it. So He said, rebuking those who are stingy with wealth and urging them to step out of it without it being obligatory: ﴿Are you apprehensive﴾, meaning: did you fear poverty, because of what Satan promises you of destitution, a fear that nearly split your hearts, ﴿that you should offer charity﴾ [i.e., by giving to the poor, who are your brethren] ﴿before your private consultation﴾, meaning, before consulting the Messenger ﷺ. He used the plural because it is more rebuking, in that it indicates that private consultations recur. This indicates that they did not fear the hardship that the Prophet ﷺ faced from this, while they did fear the act of giving charity. So He said: ﴿charities﴾. Some of them had abstained while being able, so Glorified is He showed them His mercy by abrogating it for them in this place, whereas for others the penalty for abstaining would have applied.

Since those before us, when they were charged with a difficult matter and compelled to fulfil it, such as having a mountain lifted over them, were punished if they disobeyed, He made clear the favour of this Community by lightening it for them. So He said, expressing by what may suggest that some of them had abstained despite capacity: ﴿So when﴾, meaning, then when ﴿you did not﴾, meaning, did not do what you were commanded regarding charity before the consultation, because of this apprehension, ﴿and Allah turned to you﴾, meaning, the Sovereign Most High, whose majesty requires that He punish whoever abandons His command, ﴿toward you﴾, meaning, He relented toward those who abstained while being able, toward those who gave charity, and toward those who did not find the means, returning them to their state before that, of the breadth of permission, pardon, overlooking, excuse, dispensation and lightening before the obligation; and He did not punish you for abstaining, nor for the manifest preoccupation that resulted from you. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: this lasted ten nights, then it was abrogated. Al-Kalbi said: it was only an hour of a day. In either case, it was not connected to what preceded it in revelation, though it was connected to it in recitation and placement. ﴿So establish﴾, out of gratitude for this generosity and forbearance by which He pardoned you, ﴿the prayer﴾, which is a purification for your souls and a connection for you with your Lord, ﴿and give zakat﴾, which is a cleanliness for your bodies and a purification and growth for your wealth and a bond with your brethren. Do not be negligent in any of that, lest you neglect it. The prayer is a light that guides to worldly and otherworldly aims and aids in the calamities of both abodes, and charity is a proof of the soundness of intention in prayer.

Since He singled out the most noble of physical acts of worship and the highest of financial rites, He generalized, urging an increase in light and proof, by which harmony in character is achieved, so that intimate communion occurs with the greatest turning toward Him and the greatest expenditure. So He said: ﴿And obey Allah﴾, meaning, the One to whom all perfection belongs, Who did not share with anyone in originating you in what you are upon, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose greatness derives from His greatness in all that he commands, for he commands you, for the honour of your Messenger ﷺ, only with the easy monotheistic disposition (hanifiyyah samhah), and He made preserving that equal to what He commanded you, then abrogated it for you regarding putting charity before consultation.

Since He had pardoned a matter which the context indicated involved negligence, and that might have led to violating sacred limits, He instilled awe of His presence by encompassing knowledge, and He expressed it as a statement of fact, because the beginning of the verse rebuked a hidden matter, and He did not emphasize it by fronting the prepositional phrase, since it contains manifest matters. So He said, conjoining to what is implied, meaning: so Allah loves those who obey: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning, He who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning, what you renew of doing, He knows its inner aspects just as He knows its outer ones.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 14:

When He had informed of the encompassing of His knowledge, as a deterrent for those who are deceived by the length of His forbearance, He indicated this by His awareness of the hypocrisy of the hypocrites, which is the most hidden of things. So He said, expressing wonder, inspiring awe, and magnifying the station by directing the address to the highest of creation (ﷺ), as an alert that none grasps this as it should be grasped except him: ﴿Have you not seen﴾. He indicated their distance from good by the particle of extent (ilaa, "to"), saying: ﴿those who have taken as allies﴾, meaning they strained to their utmost effort to make allies of those who would manage their affairs for them, ﴿a people﴾ with whom they sought honour, deceived by the strength that appeared to them from them. ﴿Allah has become angry﴾, meaning the King (p-386) the Most High, to whom there is no equal, ﴿with them﴾, meaning with those who take them as allies and those who are taken as allies, because they severed what was between them and Him. The first are the hypocrites, who took the Jews as allies. He increased the reproach against them by His words, in a resumed statement: ﴿They are not of you﴾, meaning the Jews, upon whom is anger, ﴿O believers﴾, so that you would ally with them out of fear of the sword and desire for peace, ﴿nor of them﴾, meaning the hypocrites, so that their alliance with them would be due to an earlier love and an intertwined kinship, so that this would serve them as an excuse. Rather, they are wavering (mudhabdhabun), with the believers by their words and with the disbelievers by their hearts. So they only allied with them out of passionate attachment to hypocrisy, due to the closeness of what is between them in it. Or the meaning is: the hypocrites who ally themselves are neither of the Muslims nor of the Jews who are allied with. He increased the reproach against them with the most vile of things, which drives to every vice, so He said, mentioning their state in this alliance: ﴿And they swear﴾, meaning the hypocrites renew their oath to continue, and the particle of elevation (ʿalā, "upon") indicates that they are in the utmost audacity in persisting in false oaths, the sense being: presuming ﴿upon falsehood﴾ in the claim of Islam and other things of the great sins into which they fall. So when they are rebuked for it, they hasten to oaths.

Since falsehood (kadhib) may be used in the language for what contradicts reality even if unintentionally, such as when the swearer is ignorant that his statement does not correspond to reality, He said (p-387), negating that and clarifying that they dared to swear the ghamus oath (the deliberately false oath that plunges its swearer into sin): ﴿while they know﴾, meaning that they are lying, so they are deliberate. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "A man will enter upon you whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil." Then 'Abd Allah ibn Nabtal entered, and he was blue-eyed, dark-skinned, short, with sparse beard. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" He swore by Allah that he had not done so. He said to him: "You did." So he brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not reviled him, and it was then that the verse was revealed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 15:

When he had informed about their state, he followed it with information about their outcome, saying, indicating (as al-Qushayri said) [that] whoever allies himself with one upon whom the Wrath (al-ghadab) has fallen makes himself a partner in deserving the wrath of the One who is wrathful toward him. Whoever takes as ally one upon whom Allah has sent His wrath has merited the wrath of Allah, and that is sufficient as humiliation, sorrow, and deprivation, expressing it in a way that indicates the matter has already been settled: ﴿Allah has prepared﴿ i.e., the One who possesses overwhelming majesty, so that there is no equal to Him, and He expressed it in a way that indicates mockery of them, saying: ﴿for them a punishment﴾ i.e., a matter that cuts off all sweetness ﴿severe﴾, whoever sees it and sees them knows that their very selves are drawn toward it and too weak to bear it.

When He informed of their punishment, He gave its cause in a way that indicates it is occurring in its fullest form, saying, emphasizing the denunciation of those who used to find their deeds pleasing: ﴿Indeed, they—evil is what﴾ i.e., it reached the extreme of what is evil, and He indicated that this was for them like a natural disposition by His saying: ﴿they used to do﴾ i.e., they continually renewed their deeds, persisting in them without ever ceasing from them: their deceit toward the believers, their counsel to the disbelievers, their defaming of Islam and its people, their audacity in false oaths, and they persisted in that until the habituation to it increased them in boldness toward all sins.

When this clause indicated their evil deeds and their persistence in them, He emphasized that with His saying: ﴿They have taken﴾, meaning they imposed upon their original, upright natures, because of the deep-rootedness they had in crookedness of disposition and their love of harm, ﴿their oaths﴾, the false ones, which are not made light of by one in whose heart there is an atom's weight of a mustard seed of faith, ﴿as a shield﴾, meaning a protection and a cover from everything that would expose them as hypocrites, whatever it might be, or that would make their killing obligatory because of the disbelief that issues from them.

Since their knowledge that He is pleased with them for their outward conduct and accepts their oaths was what emboldened them toward great wrongs, and since they used to make people desire hypocrisy for the sake of immediate appetites, and discourage them from the religion with its immediate burdens and deferred rewards, He based on the acceptance of their faith the statement, showing it openly with added rebuke [to them]: ﴿So they averted﴾, meaning that the acceptance of this from them and the postponement of their punishment became a cause for their bringing about the averting ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, meaning the law of the Supreme King, which is the path to His good pleasure, which is the cause of the greatest success. For they would discourage whomever they met from entering Islam, belittle its affair and disparage it. And whoever saw them escape hardships by their deceitful oaths, and whose provisions were restored to them as a respite, and who gained elevation among people through their statements, which they confirmed with oaths to please people, was deluded by that and followed their custom in their words and deeds, and wove on their loom, being deceived by the outward appearance of their affair, turning away from what Allah, glorified is He, had threatened them with as the recompense of their deception and their scheming. He treated the matter in the style of mockery, using the lam that is used for what is beloved, and said: ﴿Then for them﴾, meaning that as a consequence of their averting, there was for them ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾, as a recompense for their seeking, through that averting, to exalt themselves and to humiliate the people of Islam.

Since they had wealth and children in which they took pride, He said, beginning a new statement [indicating] that whoever shelters behind a shield other than His obedience, so that his worldly life may be safe behind him, will have his shelter exposed to the arrows of divine decree from where he does not perceive, so that neither his religion remains nor his worldly life is safe: ﴿Their wealth will not avail them at all﴾, i.e., in no way whatsoever, ﴿nor their children﴾ (the negation is repeated to specify each of the two), i.e., in the world or in the Hereafter, whether by ransom or otherwise. ﴿Against Allah﴾, i.e., in giving any sufficiency originating from the Supreme King, to whom there is no equal, ﴿in anything﴾, i.e., of sufficiency, even if very slight. Whatever He, glory be to Him, intends for them comes to pass, takes effect and proceeds, and nothing can repel it. This refutes those among them who said: "If there is a Day of Resurrection, we will surely be happier in it than you, just as we are now, and we will be helped by ourselves, our wealth and our children."

When sufficiency originating from Allah has been negated, with its negation every other sufficiency is negated, and this produces His saying: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾, i.e., the ones far removed from all good. When companionship has conveyed constant attachment, He emphasized it with His saying: ﴿They﴾, i.e., exclusively, since the punishment of others is dwarfed, because of their being in the abyss, compared to their punishment, ﴿therein﴾, i.e., exclusively, without anything falling short of it, ﴿will abide forever﴾, i.e., remain, persist, endure and be constant without end.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 18:

Since their corruption of the bonds between people (dhat al-bayn) was done in secret, and their oath denying that, openly, was combined with the obligation to accept what had appeared of it from them, while He, glory be to Him and exalted, knows that they lied, (it was) enraging and painful. And perhaps someone might have imagined that He, just as He obliged us to accept what appeared from them in the abode of action, would command accepting them in the abode of recompense, (so) He said, negating that (p-391) and consoling the believers, that they will do that with Him, glory be to Him, after the veil is lifted and matters are made clear, because a person is raised upon what he died upon, since that is his innate nature from which he cannot be separated, and that will not benefit them. Mentioning the time of eternity and the manifestation of punishment: ﴿On the Day when Allah raises them all﴾, that is, the King who possesses all attributes of perfection, by bringing them back to life from the death they were in and returning them to what they were before ﴿all together﴾, leaving none of them, nor of others, except that He returns him to what he was [upon] before his death. ﴿Then they will swear﴾, that is, as a consequence of the manifestation of complete power over them and their witnessing what they used to deny, of resurrection and the Fire, that they will swear ﴿to Him﴾, that is, to Allah in the Hereafter, that they are Muslims, and so they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23] and similar lies which only increase them in harm and do not avail them anything in any way, following what they were disposed to: preferring desire and being limited in looking at the sensible things they were accustomed to. ﴿As they swear﴾ in the world ﴿to you﴾, because you do not know the unseen, while expecting that Allah will expose them, as He did for them repeatedly, and their oath arises from the belief that they are far from acceptance, for no one swears to you except one who thinks you will disbelieve him. Al-Qushayri said: Their greatest punishment is their thinking it is alien, and the utmost effort is their being overturned on their faces into the pit of their regret. (p-392) Since what drives them to undertake that is the weakness of their intellects, their excessive immersion in hypocrisy, and their persistence in it until they are raised upon the like of that, while knowing that this will not save them because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, glory be to Him, He expressed it with ﴿they suppose﴾, indicating that they are at the extreme of ignorance and lack of intellect. ﴿And they suppose﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, by their false oaths, ﴿that they are upon something﴾, that is, something by which they would gain benefit, imagining that their oaths will pass with Allah and so save them, as they did save them in the world.

Since this implies that their affairs have no reality, neither in their reports, nor in their oaths, nor in their supposing, [He said, calling out against them, emphasizing the refutation of their supposing]: ﴿Unquestionably, they are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the liars﴾, that is, those judged to be liars in their supposing and in their reports in both abodes, because of their long practice in the attribute of lying, since they are not ashamed of lying before Allah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 19:

When this absorption in what is of no benefit had reached the point where, for a listener, it is extremely strange that a person of sound intellect would fall into it even once in his life, let alone persist in it, he informed about what drives them to it, saying, beginning a new sentence: ﴿Satan has gained mastery over them﴾. That is, he sought to overpower, drive, hasten, herd, incite, subdue, and take control, ﴿over them, Satan﴾, even though he is cast out and burned. All of this was carried out by him, he reached what he wanted from them, and he took possession of them in a way that left them no choice. So they became his subjects and his fief, and he surrounded them from every side, dominating them outwardly and inwardly. This derives from their saying: "I took the camels" (ḥudtu al-ibil), meaning I gained control over them, and "the donkey herded the wild-ass herd" (ḥāẓa al-ḥimār al-ʿānah), when he gathered it and drove it, dominating it. Al-ḥawdh is fast driving, and from it comes al-aḥwadhī (the nimble one), meaning one light in walking because of his skill. It came in its original form, following the rule of the sound verbs, because it was not formed from ḥāza in the manner of iftaqara, for there is no bare form of it; they did not say faqara. ﴿So He caused them to forget﴾, that is, as a consequence of his gaining mastery over them, he caused them to forget ﴿the remembrance of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong the Most Beautiful Names and the Highest Attributes, after His remembrance had been fixed in their original nature (fiṭar), so that they no longer remember Him at all, neither with the heart nor with the tongue.

When this had occurred, it inevitably produced his statement: ﴿Those﴾, that is, those who have placed themselves in the lowest position, ﴿are the party of Satan﴾, that is, his followers, his army, his group, his faction, his companions, those who surround him and gather around him to defend against what befalls and oppresses him (ḥazabahu, meaning it struck him and was severe upon him), the ones who are distanced and burned, because they followed him and did not fear blame from anyone in his requital and the execution of what he wants. Yet he is entirely deficiency and defect, while they are inclined by nature to hate him, and they abandoned the One who possesses all perfection, whose remembrance and love are fixed in their natures. Therefore the summary and the result of this is his statement: (p-394) ﴿Unquestionably﴾, and he emphasized it because they assume profit from what they have in this world of abundance, the visible solidarity, and the respite of expansion and ease. So he said: ﴿Indeed, the party of Satan﴾, that is, the cast-out and burned one, ﴿they﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿are the losers﴾, that is, those utterly ruined in this description, because they gained nothing but expulsion and burning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 20:

When he had explained what loss the forgetting of the Remembrance (dhikr) had led them to, he explained that it had caused them to fall into enmity. So, giving the reason for the loss, the forgetting and the factionalism, and emphasizing (this) as a refutation of their swearing to the negation of that, he made the place of the pronoun explicit in order to draw attention to the attribute that brings about destruction: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose⦗ —the idgham (assimilation of the two identical letters) may be for concealing that faith— and it is understood from it that the ruling applies, by a fortiori reasoning, to whoever openly opposes⦘ ﴿Allah﴾, meaning: they act toward the Supreme King, to whom none is equal, as one acts who contends with another over a land and prevails over a part of it, so he sets a boundary for it that his adversary cannot transgress. ﴿And His Messenger﴾, whose greatness derives from His greatness.

And since they do not do this except because of the abundance of their helpers and followers, so that whoever sees them thinks that they are the mighty ones, there is no one mightier than them, Allah, exalted is He, said, negating this apparent delusion: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the remote and the lowest, ﴿are among the most humbled﴾ [i.e.] (p-395) those who know that they are the most abject of creation, such that each of them is described as the most abject absolutely, without any being preferred over him, so that it encompasses every one to whom abasement can apply. This holds in this world and the Hereafter, whether they were Persia and Rome or greater than them, whether they were disbelieving kings or sinners, as al-Hasan said: "Indeed, for disobedience there is abasement in their hearts, even if the bridles rattle with them."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 58, verse 21:

When He caused them to descend to the lowest of the low, He gave the reason for that [by what indicates] that He, glory be to Him, has no partner in fulfilling His words by granting victory to His allies despite their weakness, and abandoning His enemies despite their strength, because He, glory be to Him, is a pure [unseen] being, with no indication of Him except through His acts. Thus He said: ﴿Allah has decreed﴾, that is, He acted as one who has settled a matter, finished with it, and written it down, so He made it binding, decisive, final and conclusive. ﴿That I shall surely prevail﴾, i.e., the One who is the King, to whom none is equal. The emphasis (in ﴿Surely I shall prevail﴾) is against what they supposed of victory through numbers and strength. ﴿I and My messengers﴾, that is, through the power of argument and the strength of combat. So He is truthful in relation to the one sent with war and to the one sent with proof. He gave the reason for this subjugation by His saying, emphasizing it, because their actions toward His allies are the actions of one who supposes their weakness: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ [that is,] the One to whom all command belongs, ﴿Powerful﴾. He pours forth from the inner reality of His strength (p-396) what manifests the outward power of His allies. For the powerful is one who has inner self-sufficiency, by which he bears what the one undertaking the matter carries, even if burdens were multiplied upon him to whatever extent they might be multiplied; and his protection from what approaches majesty is by a severity and a seizing arising from that inner self-sufficiency. Whatever appears of the effect of that is power. So no ability appears from creation except by relying on the strength that is in Allah, and no true standing of inner reality exists except through Allah, in whose hand is the dominion of everything. Therefore, in truth, there is no powerful one except Him.

Since the powerful among created beings may be surpassed by others, even if only at a time, He negated that with His saying: ﴿Mighty﴾, that is, Victorious with a victory in which the defeated finds no kind of resistance or escape, and this attribute belongs to Him always.

[p. 397] Since it has become clear, as plain as the sun, that whoever is allied with Allah (glorified is He) is successful, and whoever opposes Him is a loser, the necessary result is a definite warning against allying with the enemies of Allah. This is expressed in the context of negation, which conveys emphasis in forbidding it and in deterring people from drawing near to it. So He says: ﴿You will not find﴾, meaning after this explanation, ﴿a people﴾, meaning people who have the power to do what they want to attempt, ﴿who believe﴾, meaning who renew their faith and maintain it, ﴿in Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses the Most Beautiful Names and the Sublime Attributes, ﴿and the Last Day﴾, which is the place of recompense for every doer for everything he has done, the place where wisdom is manifested, ﴿loving﴾ [p. 397] meaning that there arises from them affection, neither outwardly nor inwardly. This is indicated by the idgham (assimilation of the two identical letters in the verb), and its least degree is agreement in supporting them. ﴿those who oppose Allah﴾, meaning who oppose the Supreme King by hostility in matters of limits. Therefore, opposition is not hidden, even if it is inward and its doer conceals it, because the outward is the sign of the inward, and actions are evidence of statements. This compels greater aversion from them. ﴿and His Messenger﴾, for whoever opposes him has opposed the One who sent him. Indeed, you will find them only opposing them, not loving them. He adds emphasis to this by His saying: ﴿even if they were their fathers﴾, whom Allah has made obligatory for their children to obey in what is right, as Abu 'Ubaydah 'Amir ibn al-Jarrah (may Allah be pleased with him) did when he killed his father 'Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah on the Day of Uhud; ﴿or their sons﴾, whom they were created to love and be merciful toward, as Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) did when he called his son to a duel on the Day of Badr. He said: "Leave me, O Messenger of Allah, let me be in the first vanguard." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Let us enjoy you with yourself, O Abu Bakr. Do you not know that you are to me like my hearing and my sight?"; ﴿or their brothers﴾ [who are] their supporters, [p. 398] as Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr (may Allah be pleased with him) did when he killed his brother 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr on the Day of Uhud. And Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) broke through the ranks that day, repeatedly targeting his brother 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas in order to kill him, but 'Utbah evaded him like a fox. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade him and said: "Do you want to kill yourself?" And Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him) killed his foster brother Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, the Jew, the chief of Banu al-Nadir; ﴿or their kinsfolk﴾, who are their helpers and supporters, as 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) did when he killed his maternal uncle al-'As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah on the Day of Badr. 'Ali, Hamzah and 'Ubaydah ibn al-Harith (may Allah be pleased with them) killed on the Day of Badr their paternal cousins 'Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah. It is also related from al-Thawri that the salaf (the early generations) used to hold that the verse was revealed concerning those who keep company with the ruler. The end of the quotation. The core of all this is that a person must cut off his hope from anyone other than Allah; if he does not, he is not sincere in his faith.

Since nothing leads to disavowal of such people except pure faith, He brings forth His saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the most exalted in rank and the highest in aspiration, ﴿He has written﴾ [p. 399] meaning He has joined and established [faith] as a firm connection, like the bead in the leather and the embroidery in the woven garment, so there is no separation from it. ﴿faith in their hearts﴾, making them its receptacles, so that this produced the light of the inner self and the uprightness of outward deeds. ﴿and strengthened them﴾, meaning He fortified them, reinforced them, helped them, encouraged them, magnified them and honored them ﴿with a spirit﴾, meaning a very noble light by which they comprehend what He placed in His Book and in the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) of treasures of knowledge and action. So it is to their hearts what the spirit is to the bodies. Therefore they do not do anything of the ways of the people of ignorance, such as alliance with the disbelievers. He added nobility to this strengthening by His saying: ﴿from Him﴾, meaning He gave them life through it, so there is no separation from it for them at any time. Thus there resulted for them uprightness of methods, outwardly and inwardly. They overcame by proofs and arguments, and they prevailed by the sword that destroys souls, and they performed righteous deeds, so they became lamps for the world. Therefore, you will find nothing more effective in sincerity than allying with the friends of Allah and opposing His enemies. Indeed, it is the very essence of sincerity. Whoever inclines toward one who deviates from His religion, or flatters an innovator in his creed, Allah will strip the light of monotheism from his heart.

Since He had informed them of what He gave them in this world, which will not leave them in the Hereafter, He informed them of what He will bestow on them in the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿And He will admit them to gardens﴾, meaning orchards [p. 400] whose interior is concealed by the abundance of their trees. He informed about their irrigation by His saying: [﴿flowing﴾. And since water, if it covered the earth, would leave no place to settle, He stated the preposition, and said]: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning therefore they are abundant in gardens, trees, open spaces and dwellings. Since this pleasure is only enjoyed when it is everlasting, He said: ﴿abiding therein﴾. Since this cannot be complete except with the pleasure of its owner, He said: ﴿Allah is pleased﴾, meaning the Supreme King, to whom all command belongs, so there is no turning to anyone else, ﴿with them﴾. And since this cannot have full joy except with their pleasure, so that the goodness of the neighborhood may be complete, He said: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, because He has given them beyond what they hoped for. Since He had informed about them with what delights every hearer, so that he longs for their company, their association, their fellowship and their closeness, He praised them and made them known by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning those who are in the highest rank of greatness, because they restricted their affection to Allah, knowing that benefit [and harm] is only in His hand. ﴿are the party of Allah﴾, meaning the troops of the Supreme King, whose [power] encompasses all the attributes of perfection, and His friends. Indeed, they become angry for His sake and do not fear the blame of any blamer in His cause. Since it became clear from what He prepared for them and prepared for their opposites that they are the ones exclusively possessing every good, He said, as a conclusion from what preceded, emphasizing the misery of their opponents: ﴿Surely, the party of Allah﴾, meaning the troops of the Supreme King, who are these described ones and whoever [p. 401] allies with them, ﴿they are﴾, meaning exclusively and no others, ﴿the successful﴾, meaning those who have attained victory in everything they hope for in both abodes. It has been understood from the mutual pleasure, the partisanship and the success that they are never separated from happiness. This makes it unnecessary to restrict the eternity of their abiding with the word "everlasting." He singled them out with this because He possesses might, power, knowledge and wisdom. Therefore He knew the matter of the woman who disputed (with the Prophet), and had mercy on her complaint, because she belongs to His party, and He heard her. Whoever is heard by Him is pleased with Him. He forbade zihar (the pre-Islamic formula of divorce by equating a wife with one's mother) on account of her complaint, honoring her with His wisdom, because it contradicts wisdom, being a comparison outside the rules of comparisons. In it there is also degradation of the mother, who in His religion has the utmost honor, by equating her with a wife, who is the place of lying with. He concluded its verses by stating that whoever transgresses His limits and returns to the ways of the Jahiliyyah is opposing Him (glorified is He), and is therefore of the party of Satan. Thus its end returns to its beginning, with the clearest proof of the best path, because this glorious Qur'an is the most noble speech and the most upright saying. This is the aim of what follows it. There is no doubt that it necessitates His transcendence, far removed from association and likeness. So glorified is He who revealed it as a sign whose clarity is perpetual, which necessitates faith, which suppresses rebellion, throughout the ages and the lengthening of times.
